title: Space bound for sequential machine composition
statement: Let $S,T$ be sets, let $k\in\mathbb N$, and let $R,Q$ be machines with $k$ work tapes and Boolean symbols, with exit state $e_x\in S$ for $R$ and entry state $e_y\in T$ for $Q$. Suppose configurations $d,e$ of $R$ on a Boolean input satisfy $R^a(d)=e$, the state of $e$ is $e_x$, and no earlier run $R^u(d)$ for $u<a$ has state $e_x$. Then the machine that runs $R$ until its exit state and switches to $Q$ at entry state $e_y$, started from $d$ with its states relabeled into the left side of $S\oplus T$, uses at most $\operatorname{space}_R(d,a)+\operatorname{space}_Q(e',b)$ space through time $a+1+b$, for every $b\in\mathbb N$, where $e'$ is $e$ with its state replaced by $e_y$.
hypotheses_covered: $d,e$ are configurations on the same Boolean input and $a,b\in\mathbb N$
No $u<a$ has state $e_x$ in the run from $d$
